title: The City of God
author: augustine
attributionNote: Written by Augustine over thirteen years; the work is his own, though he revised his views in the Retractations.
description: Augustine's response to the accusation that Christianity caused the sack of Rome. The first ten books answer pagan critics; the remaining twelve trace two cities, earthly and heavenly, through scripture and history.
historicalContext: Begun after the Visigothic sack of Rome in 410, and completed over thirteen years while Augustine was bishop of Hippo.
availabilityNote: Streamed from New Advent at read time. Dods's 1871 translation, served by the CCEL. The Latin original is not hosted in this streaming edition.
